# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This is the lab companion for **BIOL 202: Introduction to Biostatistics** at the University of British Columbia, Okanagan campus. It provides the R tutorials for the lab portion of the course.

It also works as a general resource for anyone learning to manage and analyze data using R and R Markdown in the RStudio IDE.

These tutorials cover the computation; the lectures and assigned course readings cover the concepts. The rule is **concept first, computation second**: an idea is introduced in the lecture or the assigned reading, and the lab tutorial then implements it in R. If a tutorial asks you to run a test, you will already have met what it is for.

This book is **a living document that is updated intermittently.** If you find errors or wish to provide feedback, please [contact me](https://jasonpither.weebly.com/people.html).

## Setting up: do this once {#setup .unnumbered}

You need three things before you start: R, RStudio, and the `biol202` package. [Tutorial 1](01-getting-started.qmd#setup) walks you through installing all three, in order — start there before anything else in this book.

## Licence {.unnumbered}

These tutorials are licensed [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/).

Many of the datasets accompany Whitlock, M. C. & Schluter, D., *The Analysis of Biological Data*, and are redistributed under the same licence their authors published them under ([Whitlock & Schluter 2018](https://qubeshub.org/publications/351/1)). Each dataset's help page records its source. Note that most of those values were digitized from figures and tables in the original publications, so they are teaching reconstructions rather than the original measurements — fine for learning, not for research.
